gap: Passage-local context-triple supervision has not been evaluated on standard multi-hop KGQA benchmarks, because those benchmarks (WebQSP and CWQ over Freebase, MetaQA over a movies KG, as used in the analyzed retrieval and intermediate-supervision works) are not packaged with source-passage provenance for their triples. Text-attributed resources that would make the mechanism constructible do exist elsewhere - triple-to-source-text traceability in GraphMERT-extracted KGs and large-scale KG-text alignment datasets such as CDTP - but they are used for KG completion and text generation rather than for measuring whether context-triple supervision transfers beyond a single synthetic, domain-specific MCQ setting.

evidence.quote: A useful property of the GraphMERT pipeline is that extracted triples are traceable to their originating source text sequence [22].
Each instance pairs a Chinese-language text with one or more textually supported KG triples, totaling 15 million triples.
First, the QA datasets used for SFT, repair, RL, and evaluation are synthetically generated.

why_unaddressed: The works that use standard benchmarks do retrieval or intermediate supervision rather than context-triple supervision, and the work that uses context-triple supervision deliberately avoided standard benchmarks by constructing its own disease-specific, synthetically generated MCQ data with GraphMERT. No retrieved paper attempts the cross-setting transfer, so the external validity of the mechanism is untested rather than refuted.
research_question: Does context-triple supervision improve multi-hop KGQA when evaluated with open-ended metrics on a text-attributed KG other than the two disease-specific ones, rather than only on synthetic domain multiple-choice items?
potential_experiment: Rebuild the context-graph supervision on a text-attributed corpus that ships triple-to-text provenance (e.g., a GraphMERT-style extraction from an open corpus, or a KG-text alignment dataset such as CDTP), generate or reuse open-ended multi-hop questions over it, and evaluate per-hop-depth exact match/F1 against the isolated-triple baseline, a retrieval-based baseline (subgraph retrieval, GNN-RAG-style), and the closest work's MCQ-style protocol.
verification_required: Whether an English-language text-attributed multi-hop KGQA benchmark with triple-level passage provenance exists was not established: the literature search budget was exhausted before this could be searched, so this must be verified by a further search (e.g., text-attributed knowledge graph QA datasets, document-grounded KGQA) before designing the experiment.
